# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b6 — Per-room Home Assistant devices

**Opt-in beta 6 — Home Assistant 2026.10+**

This beta adds a minimal, area-aware entity and device layer over the existing
environment science and climate supervisor. It is based on beta 5, including its
localization fixes, climate profiles, Home Assistant installation safeguards and
hardware safety interlocks. Stable **v0.5.1 remains unchanged**.

## One device per configured area

* Each monitored HA area gets an **`<Area> Environment`** device assigned to
  the Home Assistant area registry; enabled climate/PID-only areas are also
  included. Disabled or deleted areas are not invented.
* Each device exposes **one Environment overview sensor**, whose state is the
  calculated room assessment. Its attributes contain the original HA source
  entity IDs and raw states next to normalized values, units and availability.
  Window contact states, room advice, science estimates, occupancy/away/sleep
  diagnostics, actuator hold reasons and configured source entities are grouped
  for dashboards and templates.
* When the optional mold indicator is enabled for an air-monitoring room, the
  device additionally exposes **Surface humidity (calculated)** as a percentage
  sensor, with dew point and estimated cold-surface temperature in attributes.
  An uncalibrated or unavailable source gives an unavailable calculated value;
  it is never fabricated or treated as safe.
* The original whole-home window recommendation entity and its attributes remain
  intact, so existing dashboard cards, integrations and automations work.

## Minimal entities, no duplicated controls

This integration does **not** create duplicate numeric target-temperature
entities, temperature or humidity measurements, CO₂/PM sensors, thermostats,
fan-speed controls or humidifier setpoints. Native climate, fan, humidifier and
sensor entities retain their own complete control surfaces. The new room
overview gives dashboards a central place to read the inputs and decisions
without taking ownership of those raw devices.

The area overview is **read-only**. It does not send a setpoint or HVAC command,
change controller authorization, infer a missing measurement as zero or issue a
window actuation. Existing opt-in supervisor actions and physical safety checks
remain the sole route for managed actuation.

## Compatibility and safety

The integration domain remains `air_quality_advisor`; saved configuration
entries, existing entity unique IDs, PID pause latches, climate-room profiles,
HACS custom-repository installation and sensor routing are preserved. Only
actual HA area-registry IDs are used, and a user-assigned device area is never
silently overwritten.

Automated beta publication runs Python 3.13/3.14 tests, regenerated 38-language
locales, frontend tests, JSON/syntax checks, Hassfest and HACS validation.
The release is published as a **prerelease**, with `--latest=false`, and does
not replace the stable release. Unit tests do not constitute physical actuator
commissioning; compressor-affecting behavior and relay/fan power still require
independent hardware safety verification.

## Install with HACS

Back up your HA configuration. In the Home Environment Manager custom HACS
repository choose **Redownload → Show beta versions → v0.6.0b6**, then restart
Home Assistant. Reconfigure the *existing* entry through **Configure**, never
re-add it as a second integration. If a HACS prerelease is not offered, use the
manual-install ZIP attached to this beta release, extracting
`custom_components/air_quality_advisor/` into your HA configuration.

This release retains international sensor support, the optional Announcement
Hub routing, room-specific window advice, advanced environmental science and
localized setup explanations from previous versions. New area entities are a
read-only way to observe the same decisions, not an alternative controller.
